Technical Details about Implementation: Specific items asking for a designated response (e.g., 'choose strongly disagree') to detect failure to follow content. Scoring is binary based on whether the requested response is selected.
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): High accuracy for identifying blatant carelessness; easily scoreable with little ambiguity.

Technical Details about Implementation: Insertion of items describing logical impossibilities (e.g., 'I am paid by leprechauns') to detect agreement. Detection of nonsensical responses indicates invalidity.
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): Moderate to High; better at catching 'savvy' respondents than instructed items but may produce false positives (highly diligent respondents associating items metaphorically).

Technical Details about Implementation: Measuring the time elapsed per survey page. Uses a minimum threshold, typically recommended at 2 seconds per item, to identify impossibly fast completions.
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): High; very effective for detecting 'rushing' and difficult for respondents to elude if not explicitly told time is being tracked.

Technical Details about Implementation: A count of the maximum number of consecutive identical responses or identical response patterns (straight-lining). Usually uses a cutoff score (e.g., 0.4 SD above sample mean).
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): High for invariant types; Meade & Craig (2012) found it effective for identifying specific non-random patterns.

Technical Details about Implementation: Multivariate outlier analysis that assesses the distance of a respondent's data point from the centroid of the sample distribution. Utilizes a chi-square statistic for cutoff scores.
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): High; among the best for identifying random responses and multiple types of outliers across all items.

Technical Details about Implementation: Development of scales consisting of repeated items or negative versions of identified items to measure within-person response consistency (e.g., Variable/True Response Inconsistency).
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): Moderate to High; traditional psychometric standard for consistency detection.

Technical Details about Implementation: Use of an infrequency scale to detect insufficient effort responding by identifying responses that are statistically rare or highly unlikely.
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): Moderate; dependent on the quality and content of the infrequency items used.

Technical Details about Implementation: Within-person correlation between pairs of items that are theoretically similar (synonyms) or opposite (antonyms; one is reverse-coded). Pairs can also be formed statistically (Meade & Craig's method using r > 0.60).
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): Moderate to High; robust because they do not necessarily assume most of the sample is diligent.

Technical Details about Implementation: Dividing established scales into two subscales (even vs. odd items) and computing the correlation between those subscales for each individual respondent.
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): High; Meade & Craig (2012) found it among the best indicators for identifying random responding.

Technical Details about Implementation: Sophisticated models (e.g., Guttman errors) that examine the statistical likelihood of an observed response pattern given the nature of the data/item difficulty.
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): High; provides a more robust estimate than single-indicator methods but is technically complex.

Technical Details about Implementation: Repeating the pairing process (like even-odd) many times using different item subsets and averaging the results to reduce sampling error in the reliability estimate.
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): Very High; produces more robust estimates of carelessness than single-computation indices.

Technical Details about Implementation: Using multiple careless response indices as indicators in a mixture model to classify respondents into groups based on the likelihood of different types of careless responding.
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): Very High; found to yield the most promising results by considering multiple indicators simultaneously.

Technical Details about Implementation: Computed by summing the absolute differences of responses to 15 highly correlated BFI-2 item pairs (r ≥ \.50\).
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): Very high (AUC values ranging from .913 to .990)
Flag or Outright Reject: Outright Reject (scores 14-17 used as cutoff for record exclusion)

Technical Details about Implementation: Evaluation of response consistency across statistically related item pairs within the MMPI-3 framework.
Likelihood/Confidence (Inferred): High (validated in clinical and research contexts)

Technical Details about Implementation: Measures tendency to respond inconsistently via acquiescence or counter-acquiescence on specific item pairs.
Flag or Outright Reject: Outright Reject (used to identify invalid response sets)
